short: Germany's last offensive in the west, and the costliest battle in US Army history.
full:
On 16 December 1944, under fog that grounded Allied aircraft, three German armies attacked a thinly held stretch of the Ardennes with around 400,000 men and 1,400 tanks and assault guns. The objective was Antwerp, and with it the splitting of the British and American armies. Two inexperienced American divisions were overrun and the salient that gave the battle its name pushed sixty miles west. At Malmedy, SS troops shot 84 prisoners.

The road junctions held. American engineers blew bridges and denied fuel dumps to a force that had never had enough petrol, and the 101st Airborne was surrounded at Bastogne, where McAuliffe answered a German surrender demand with a single word. Patton disengaged his Third Army, turned it ninety degrees north and relieved the town on 26 December. The skies cleared, and by 25 January 1945 the Germans were back on their start line, having lost about 100,000 men and their last armoured reserve. American casualties were around 80,000.
